summary: Accepted ADR0096 distinguishes an unpublished-source local build/test/static check in a fresh isolated output/cache root, without credentials, shared/remote writes or publication/live-store/Home/VM/native effects, from the original-operation route. Such ordinary verification needs no Root runtime admission, operation identity/clock, frozen packet or pre-run peer review: the owner stays within its stated CPU/memory share, preserves first failures and reports results. Candidate source review, exact-head required CI and ADR0084 coherent validation remain required. Publication, credentials, shared effects, Home/VM/native actions, destructive/uncertain effects and plan-required acceptance retain their actual effect-specific discipline. The439 inherited and46 later originals are unrecoverable history and do not fence demonstrably isolated fresh generation/state/identity/outputs. Original outcomes remain unproved and are never replayed or assigned renewed clocks. Named live holds keep their actual owner/scope; missing relevant isolation is not empty coverage. The ADR governs the older packaged inspection copy until coherent instruction adoption. Atlas indexes this accepted decision and grants no operation authority.
title: Ordinary isolated source verification and unrecoverable-history boundaries
